atoms.text: Now Carla is going to show you around some tents and huts around the world.

instruction.text: Select the three images of tents and huts.

finish.text: Many people in villages or natural areas around the world live in tents and huts. Their homes are often smaller and simpler than houses in cities, but they still act as great shelter!

feedback.wrong: This is a house in the USA.

instruction.text: This is a tent in Morocco. Select the opening to learn more.

feedback.end: Tents are often used by nomadic people. Nomadic people don’t have a fixed home and travel around with their animals to find new grass for them. This means they need homes that can be packed up and moved around!

instruction.text: This is a tent in Mongolia. Select the door to learn more.

feedback.end: This round tent is called a yurt. It’s used by Asian nomadic people in the Eurasian Steppe, which is a region full of open grasslands. It can get very cold here, and yurts are perfect for keeping people warm!

instruction.text: This is a thatched hut in a tribal village in Western New Guinea, Indonesia. Select the wall to learn more.

feedback.end: New Guinea is home to many tribal societies, who live in villages far away from big cities and have their own rules and traditions. Their homes are usually huts made from wood and dry plants!

atoms.a: “In which of these places do you think people might live in huts?“
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f8_2025'>In which of these places do you think people might live in huts?</voice>

feedback.end: Huts are only used by people who live in villages or tribes, so they’re found in natural areas.

atoms.a: “In which of these places do you think people could set up a yurt?“
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f8_2025'>In which of these places do you think people could set up a yurt?</voice>

feedback.end: Exactly! Asian nomadic groups move around to give their animals grass to feed on, so they set up their yurts on open grasslands.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Carla has taken you to a yurt in Kyrgyzstan to see what it’s like. Can you see the following things? Select the correct answer.

feedback.finish: Homes don’t only look different on the outside, but also on the inside! You'll usually find beds and other important things in tents and huts, but you might not find individual rooms with doors.
